task: Minimize a smooth convex objective with possible nonsmooth regularization from a VOS/continuous-time perspective and verify accelerated convergence on high-dimensional Lasso data.
primary_problem: Lasso: minimize F(x)=0.5/n ||Ax-b||_2^2 + lambda ||x||_1 from x0=0.
named_method_commitments: Variable/operator splitting viewpoint: split smooth gradient operator and nonsmooth proximal/shrinkage operator; for ADMM split x=z constraint.
Nesterov acceleration from a continuous-time second-order ODE perspective with damping approximately 3/t and discrete FISTA/Nesterov momentum.
ADMM as an operator-splitting method with primal and dual residuals and an augmented-Lagrangian Lyapunov surrogate.
Strong Lyapunov functions: track objective gap plus kinetic/momentum terms for acceleration and residual/dual-energy descent for ADMM.
Linear convergence assessment where possible using empirical log-slope fits; note Lasso is not globally strongly convex because p>n, so exact theorem assumptions are restricted or empirical.
planned_algorithms: adaptive-restart FISTA as continuous-time restart-inspired linear-rate variant
primary_metrics: objective gap to best computed value
validation_requirements: compare algorithms on same lambda and x0
separate verified data results from related-work assumptions
